subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 7-year-old boy with xeroderma pigmentosum has had several severe sunburns despite limited sun exposure. Examination shows diffuse freckling, conjunctival injection, and multiple rough keratotic papules on the face and dorsal hands. His parents ask what other problems he is likely to face.
question: Which of the following is the most likely additional finding in this patient?

options.text: Squamous cell carcinomas and basal cell carcinomas of sun-exposed skin
Growth retardation with a photosensitive butterfly rash and increased sister chromatid exchanges

explanation_correct: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective nucleotide excision repair, so UV-induced pyrimidine dimers persist and mutagenesis is accelerated. Patients develop actinic keratoses and skin cancers, including squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma, on sun-exposed areas, often in childhood.

explanation_incorrect.B: Cafe-au-lait spots with pancytopenia and skeletal anomalies suggest Fanconi anemia, a crosslink repair defect.
explanation_incorrect.C: Cerebellar ataxia with conjunctival telangiectasias describes ataxia-telangiectasia, a double-strand break repair defect.
explanation_incorrect.D: Multiple adenomatous polyps suggest familial adenomatous polyposis or MUTYH-associated polyposis, not xeroderma pigmentosum.
explanation_incorrect.E: Growth retardation with a photosensitive rash and increased sister chromatid exchanges describes Bloom syndrome, a helicase defect.

educationalObjective: Xeroderma pigmentosum markedly increases the risk of skin cancers on sun-exposed areas, including squamous cell and basal cell carcinomas.
